## Every cell's citation, and what each source is actually like

### Seeed Studio — Seeed-Studio/OSHW-XIAO-Series

<https://github.com/Seeed-Studio/OSHW-XIAO-Series>

- **Shape** — one repository for the whole XIAO range
- **Size** — 196,037 KiB (L: GitHub repos API .size, 2026-08-25)
- **Licence** — MIT; covers design files (L: GitHub repos API .license.spdx_id = MIT; LICENSE at repo root)

- **Sch src**: no (A) — no .sch, .kicad_sch, .schdoc or .dsn anywhere in 675 blobs *GitHub trees API main?recursive=1, 2026-08-25*
- **Sch PDF**: no (A) — the repository holds exactly two PDFs and neither is a schematic: document/Seeed_Studio_XIAO_Slides.pdf and projects/community-diy-projects/XIAO_USE_CASE.pdf *GitHub trees API main?recursive=1, 2026-08-25*
- **PCB**: no (A) — no .kicad_pcb, .brd or .pcbdoc *GitHub trees API main?recursive=1, 2026-08-25*
- **Fp/sym**: yes (O) — 37 .kicad_mod and 1 .kicad_sym under 'Seeed Studio XIAO Series Library'. This repository already imports them; the pad coordinates in webui/boards/*.json come from here. *tools/get_seeed_hardware.sh; tools/import_kicad_board.py*
- **3D**: no (A) — no STEP, WRL or board mesh of any kind. All 13 .stl live under one path, projects/community-diy-projects/XIAO_ESP32_NTP_Clock/3d_models/, and are printable clock-case parts contributed by a user -- not board geometry and not Seeed's output. An earlier version of this cell said 'partial' on the strength of the extension tally alone; opening the paths disproved it. *GitHub trees API main?recursive=1, paths listed 2026-08-25*
- **BSP**: no (A) — no pin-definition headers; Seeed's board support ships in the Arduino core, not here *GitHub trees API main?recursive=1, 2026-08-25*

> 69 PNGs account for nearly all 196,037 KiB. tools/get_seeed_hardware.sh calls them 'pictures of a pinout, not a pinout' and fetches sparsely for that reason.

> That script's '~196 MB' and GitHub's size field are the same number: GitHub reports KiB, so 196,037 KiB is 191 MiB.

> The surprise is what is missing. Seeed is the vendor this project already vendors from, and it publishes no schematic and no PCB layout at all -- only footprints and symbols. That is why the boards here are pad maps rather than netlists, and OH-28 cannot be satisfied from this source.

> espressif/esp-dev-kits is Apache-2.0 and 827,468 KiB, and it is easy to read that as 'Espressif publishes its dev-kit hardware openly'. It does not. Across 3,631 blobs the repository holds exactly one PDF (docs/_static/espressif2.pdf, the logo) and four STEP files (enclosure parts). The Apache-2.0 grant covers example code and documentation; the design files are elsewhere, on dl.espressif.com, under no stated licence at all.

> This is the clearest licence-scope split in the survey and the reason the ticket asks whether a licence covers design files or only documentation.

### Nordic Semiconductor — nRF52840-DK hardware files 3.0.3

<https://www.nordicsemi.com/Products/Development-hardware/nRF52840-DK/Download>

- **Shape** — per-kit versioned zip, eleven prior versions kept
- **Size** — 23,729,151 bytes (O: downloaded 2026-08-25)
- **Licence** — Nordic 5-clause BSD variant; covers contested, see notes (O: License.txt inside the zip, 1,950 bytes, (c) 2010-2024 Nordic Semiconductor ASA)

- **Sch src**: yes (O) — six Altium .SchDoc sheets (cover, nRF52840 MCU, interface MCU, misc, connectors, power supply) plus pca10056.PrjPCB and pca10056.IntLib *zip listing, 61 entries, 2026-08-25*
- **Sch PDF**: yes (O) — PCA10056_Schematic_And_PCB.pdf, 12,081,929 bytes *zip listing, 2026-08-25*
- **PCB**: yes (O) — 400236.PcbDoc, 15,106,048 bytes, plus a full Production files/ tree -- 14 gerber layers, 6 drill files, pick-and-place CSV, BOM .xls, assembly drawing and laminate spec *zip listing, 2026-08-25*
- **Fp/sym**: yes (O) — pca10056.IntLib, 4,599,808 bytes -- an Altium integrated library, so symbols and footprints together in a proprietary binary *zip listing, 2026-08-25*
- **3D**: no (A) — no STEP or WRL; the .PcbDoc may embed 3D bodies but that was not opened *zip listing, 2026-08-25*
- **BSP**: no (A) — not in this package; Zephyr carries the board definition separately *zip listing, 2026-08-25*

> The conflict, recorded rather than resolved: the licence shipped with the hardware files says 'software' in every clause and forbids reverse-engineering anything supplied in binary form -- but what it is attached to is an Altium PCB project. Clause 4 further restricts use to designs built around a Nordic integrated circuit. Read literally it is a software licence stapled to a board design; read by intent it is a use grant limited to Nordic parts. Either reading rules out redistributing the files, so the practical answer is the same and the ambiguity does not need settling to act on it.

> Completeness is the highest here of any vendor surveyed: schematic source, PCB source, gerbers, drill, BOM and pick-and-place, all in one download, and the flexible NFC antenna PCB as a second project alongside.

> probe.py reports HTTP 403 for the download page and that is not a broken row: nordicsemi.com refuses non-browser clients on HEAD and on GET alike. The zip itself is served from nsscprodmedia.blob.core.windows.net and answers 200 -- which is where it was fetched from here.

> Six files in the sampled repository, and the whole board design is two of them. This is the tidiest per-board layout in the survey and the easiest to fetch selectively.

> GitHub reports the licence as NOASSERTION because licence.txt is the CC-BY-SA 3.0 legal code rather than a recognised template. The README says only 'Creative Commons Attribution/Share-Alike' with no version, so the version is a fact about the file, not about the README.

> 634 repositories at roughly 1 MB each is the opposite shape from Seeed: nothing to fetch sparsely, but 634 things to enumerate.

> Correction to this survey's first pass, which recorded EAGLE as 'proprietary binary' from the extension alone. EAGLE has written XML since version 6, so this row's schematic is machine-readable today. Three vendors were mis-recorded the same way and all three were opened to fix it -- which is precisely the failure the `opened` class exists to prevent, committed by the survey that defined it.

> No licence on the repositories that matter, Apache-2.0 on ones that do not. Under those terms the files can be read but not redistributed, so this is a fetch-never-vendor source regardless of size.

This is KiCad's per-footprint 3D library, not a model of the assembled board. > Every artefact class the ticket asks about is present, in open text formats, under a named OSI licence, in one repository per board. On the ticket's own criteria this is the best source surveyed, and it is not one of the vendors this project currently carries boards from.

> Per-repository variance again: OLIMEX/ESP32-POE-ISO has no LICENSE file, only a 'Licensee.pdf', and GitHub reports no licence for it. The sibling board is Apache-2.0. Sample per repository, never per organisation.

> Pimoroni publishes no board design files. Listed rather than omitted, because 'we checked and there is nothing' is the answer a registry needs; silence would read as 'not yet surveyed'.

> What it does publish is component libraries and software, both openly. The only Pimoroni footprints anyone can use for a whole board are third-party -- there is a community KiCad footprint for the Tiny2040 and a forum thread asking for Yukon module footprints, which is what an absent vendor library looks like from the outside.
